Read the categories with care

Four things that distort the raw counts

A child is not always the same subject as its parent. Only 67.5% of child resources classify into their parent's domain. A group called Points of Interest in Rajkot breaks into WiFi hotspots, bus stops, police stations and schools — four domains. This is why resource-level counts are worth having: the group label is often a container, not a subject.

Telangana's tags describe the upload batch, not the data. All 709 T-Fiber records carry the identical four tags Fiber optic network, Telecom, Infrastructure, GeoSpatial — including ICD medical code tables, animal taxonomy and car prices. Its industry field is equally unreliable, so domains here come from titles and descriptions.

292 Telangana records are not datasets in any useful sense — they are internal tables of the Oracle APEX and Intergraph G/Technology systems behind the T-Fiber GIS: audit logs, page templates, picklists, schema dictionaries. They sit in IT / Application System Metadata so they can be excluded rather than silently inflating the infrastructure count.

The network view counts differently from the bars. For counting, a dataset belongs to exactly one sub-domain. The relationship graph instead uses every sub-domain a dataset's title and tags match — 3,038 of 4,340 match more than one. Descriptions are excluded from that pass, because several exchanges reuse one description across an entire batch. Other spatial layers is a catch-all for records whose only signal is that they are spatial, so it links widely by construction.

The tags that define each domain

Most frequent publisher tags per domain, with the boilerplate T-Fiber tag set excluded. Counts are datasets carrying that tag.

Harvested from the catalogue APIs of MahaAgX, TGDeX, DX GeoSpatial and IUDX COS; child resources via /cat/v1/relationship?id=<parent>&rel=resource. Domains are assigned by rule from each record's own title, description and tags — titles are weighted above descriptions, since several publishers reuse one description across a whole batch. Four Geospatial groups returned no children and are retained as groups so nothing is lost. Exported alongside this page as datasets_leaf_catalogue.csv.
